questions: Do your eyes ever move involuntarily or “shake” without you trying to move them?
Do your eyes ever become misaligned, with one eye drifting up, down, inward, or outward?
Do you see double when this happens?
Is this problem new or noticeably worsening?
Does it become more noticeable when you are tired, stressed, or looking at something closely?
Do you have blurred or reduced vision in either eye?
Do you have eye pain, redness, swelling, or light sensitivity?
Do you have drooping of either eyelid?
Do you have headaches, dizziness, nausea, weakness, numbness, or trouble walking?
Have you recently had a head injury, eye injury, infection, or started a new medication?
results: 1. smooth pursuit and saccades: rapid conjugate HORIZONTAL saccadic oscillations WITHOUT intersaccadic intervals - ocular flutter
2. anti-ganglioside antibodies (GQ1b, GT1a, GM1, GM2): ISOLATED anti-GT1a IgG POSITIVE; anti-GQ1b, anti-GM1 and anti-GM2 all NEGATIVE
3. CT chest / abdomen / pelvis (occult tumour): no malignancy - argues against a paraneoplastic cause
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-GT1a IgG–associated autoimmune ocular flutter, likely postinfectious and within the anti-ganglioside/Miller Fisher spectrum

ALTERNATIVE: Drug- or toxin-induced ocular flutter

ALTERNATIVE: Paraneoplastic ocular flutter/opsoclonus syndrome

ALTERNATIVE: Structural brainstem or cerebellar lesion causing saccadic oscillations
